subject: Hold on collection: unexpected mid-cycle usage & VAT handling
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy@ledgerly.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle spike on 5/18 — requesting hold on collection

Hi Marcus,

Hope you’re well. We just received the invoice for the May billing period and noticed a large jump in token consumption on 2028-05-18 that doesn’t match any activity on our side. Our engineering team checked and there were no release changes or batch replays scheduled that day.

Ledgerly is placing a temporary hold on payment for the disputed portion while we coordinate — can Redwood provide an exported usage log (request ids + timestamps + model variant) covering 05/15–05/20? We need the raw evidence so we can reconcile internally and resolve VAT implications for the EU entity.

Attached: none in this mail — I’ll follow up with the CSV if helpful.

Thanks,
Amy Chen
Billing Lead, Ledgerly Inc
amy@ledgerly.com
+44 20 7XX XXXX
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle spike on 5/18 — requesting hold on collection

Hi Amy — thanks for flagging this and for the heads-up about the payment hold.

We’ll run a focused extract for 2028-05-15 — 2028-05-20 that includes: request_id, customer_api_key (hashed), model_id, variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, region, node_id, and trace_id where available. Ben, Grace — can you take ownership of the forensic extract and share an interim CSV back to Amy today? If we see a clear pattern (staging key, replay, or misattribution) we can provisionally credit the disputed amount and pause collection while Ledgerly completes VAT coordination.

Amy — two quick clarifying Qs for our triage: 1) Is the traffic coming from a fixed set of IPs or from multiple hosts? 2) Do you have a request id or example timestamp from your side we should match against?

I’ll keep this thread as the single source of truth for the billing hold.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Chen <amy@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T12:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle spike on 5/18 — requesting hold on collection

On 5/21/28 10:05 AM, Marcus Lin wrote:
> Ben, Grace — can you take ownership of the forensic extract and share an interim CSV back to Amy today?

Working on it. I pulled a scoped export and attached the CSV stub here (usage_export_20280515-20280520.csv). The extract includes request_id, timestamp_utc, model, variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, region, node_id, and customer_key_hash. Early observations: there are ~18k extra tokens on 2028-05-18 attributed to a hashed key that resolves to a sandbox prefix we’ve historically seen in replay tests.

Next steps I recommend:
- Grace, can we validate if that hashed key is a Ledgerly staging key (they sometimes append "-stg")?
- If it’s a sandbox/test key, propose a provisional credit equal to the disputed tokens x unit price and hold collection for that line item immediately.

I’ll drop the full export into the shared drive link and notify Marcus/Amy when done.

Attachments: usage_export_20280515-20280520.csv (partial), api-req-sample.json (sample request payload)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Amy Chen <amy@ledgerly.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle spike on 5/18 — requesting hold on collection

Thanks Ben — that CSV is extremely helpful. We confirm the time window and the hashed key pattern match an internal staging process run by our SRE team (a misconfigured cron job re-ran a replay at scale). I’ve attached our local audit snippet and the exported request id sample for cross-checks.

Two VAT items to resolve before we close the loop:
1) Because this usage occurred under our EU legal entity, Ledgerly will need the corrected invoice showing the credited amount and VAT recalculated (reverse charge vs. standard VAT depending on the transaction).
2) We need the invoice hold confirmed in writing so our AP team does not auto-release payment to collections.

Attachments: invoice_20280520.pdf (original), ledgerly-audit-snippet.txt (local evidence)

If Redwood can issue a provisional credit and a corrected invoice draft (PDF) we’ll reprocess the remainder immediately.

Best,
Amy Chen
Billing Lead, Ledgerly Inc
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle spike on 5/18 — requesting hold on collection

Amy — thanks for the confirmation and for sending your audit snippet. Summary and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Finding: Ben’s export and Ledgerly’s audit align — the 2028-05-18 spike maps to a staging/replay key.
2) Provisional credit: Redwood will apply a provisional credit for the disputed token consumption (tokens x unit price) on invoice 2028-05-20. That credit will be itemized as "Staging replay credit — provisional" and will appear as a negative line on a corrected invoice draft.
3) VAT handling: Grace, can you please generate a corrected invoice draft that recalculates VAT under the EU reverse charge flow and attach for Amy? Amy — once Grace shares the draft, our tax team will sign off; the provisional credit will be applied regardless of VAT finalization so Ledgerly’s AP can proceed with the non-disputed remainder.
4) Collection hold: Redwood acknowledges the hold on collection for the credited portion. We will not escalate to collections while the credit and VAT adjustments are processed.

Deliverables and timeline: Ben will upload the full forensic CSV to the shared drive (done). Grace will send a corrected invoice draft and an internal tax sign-off note within 24 hours. Marcus will confirm when the provisional credit posts (expected within 48 hours).

If anything changes on your side please update this thread. Appreciate the quick coordination — aiming to close this before your next pay cycle.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
